title: BIO 201 : ( UNIZIK ) : SEX DETERMINATION AND SEX LINKAGE
subject: BIO 201

questions.question: Gender categorization based on reproductive roles is called which term?
questions.explanation: Sex explains the gender categorization of organisms based on the reproductive roles they play in their species.

questions.question: Organisms with male and female reproductive organs in the same individual are described as which?
questions.explanation: The condition where male and female reproductive organs exist in the same individuals is called monoecious.

questions.question: Organisms with distinct separate male and female individuals are described as which?
questions.explanation: When there are organisms of distinct sexes or separate male and female individuals, the condition is referred to as dioecious.

questions.question: Chromosomes concerned with sex determination are known as which type?
questions.explanation: Sex chromosomes or allosomes are concerned with sex determination.

questions.question: Chromosomes concerned with other body characters are known as which type?
questions.explanation: Autosomes are not concerned with sex determination but with other body characters.

questions.question: Which chromosomal sex determining system is found in mammals and plants?
questions.explanation: The XX-XY system is found in mammals and plants.

questions.question: Which chromosomal sex determining system is found in grasshoppers?
questions.explanation: The XX-XO system is found in non-heteromorphous organisms like grasshoppers.

questions.question: Which chromosomal sex determining system is found in birds and snakes?
questions.explanation: The ZZ-ZW system is found in birds, fish, snakes, amphibians, butterflies and isopods.

questions.question: The female gamete contains which chromosomes in the X-Y system?
questions.explanation: In the X-Y system the female gamete contains 2X chromosomes.

questions.question: The male gamete contains which chromosomes in the X-Y system?
questions.explanation: The male gamete contains X and Y chromosomes in the X-Y system.

questions.question: Offspring sex in the X-Y system depends on which gamete?
questions.explanation: The sex of an offspring depends on whether the sperm that fertilizes the egg cell carries an X or Y chromosome.

questions.question: Which gene on the Y chromosome determines maleness?
questions.explanation: The location of the SRY gene in the sex determining region of the Y chromosome determines maleness.

questions.question: The sex of an offspring depends on whether the fertilizing sperm carries which chromosome?
questions.explanation: An offspring develops into a female when the sperm carries an X chromosome and into a male when it carries a Y chromosome.

questions.question: Sex determination in Drosophila follows which system?
questions.explanation: In Drosophila, the female has two X chromosomes and the male has one X chromosome, following the XX-XO system.

questions.question: Which ratio determines sex in the X-O system?
questions.explanation: The ratio of X chromosomes to the number of autosomal sets determines sex in the X-O system.

questions.question: A ratio of 0.5 in X-O insects results in which sex?
questions.explanation: If an insect has an X to autosome ratio of 0.5 it will become male.

questions.question: A ratio of 1 in X-O insects results in which sex?
questions.explanation: If an insect receives two X chromosomes and is diploid the ratio is 1 and the insect will be female.

questions.question: In the Z-W system the male is described as which?
questions.explanation: In the Z-W system the male has ZZ chromosomes and is homogametic.

questions.question: In the Z-W system the female is described as which?
questions.explanation: In the Z-W system the female is heterogametic with ZW chromosomes.

questions.question: Which gamete determines the sex of the offspring in the Z-W system?
questions.explanation: In the Z-W system the ovum of the female determines the sex of the offspring.

questions.question: Who proposed the genic balance theory of sex determination?
questions.explanation: Bridges proposed the genic balance theory of sex determination in 1925.

questions.question: Genes for females are located on which chromosome?
questions.explanation: In the genic balance theory, genes for females are located on the X chromosome while those for males are located in the autosomes.

questions.question: Which ratio determines sex in genic sex determination?
questions.explanation: The ratio of X chromosomes to autosome sets determines the sex index ratio.

questions.question: A sex index value of 0.5 determines which sex?
questions.explanation: A sex index value of 0.5 and below determines maleness.

questions.question: A sex index value of 1 or more determines which sex?
questions.explanation: If the sex index value is 1 or more it is female.

questions.question: Which environmental factor affects sexual phenotypes in turtles and crocodiles?
questions.explanation: Temperature affects the sexual phenotypes of some individuals like alligators, turtles and crocodiles.

questions.question: Warm temperature produces which sex in turtles?
questions.explanation: Warm temperature produces females in turtles.

questions.question: Cold temperature produces which sex in turtles?
questions.explanation: Cold temperature produces males in turtles.

questions.question: Warm temperature produces which sex in alligators?
questions.explanation: Warm temperature produces males in alligators.

questions.question: Position in the stack determines sex in which organism?
questions.explanation: In limpets, the position in the stack determines sex.

questions.question: Who proposed the nutrition theory of sex determination?
questions.explanation: Sharp proposed the nutrition theory of sex determination in 1934.

questions.question: Big roots rich in nutrients give which flowers in Arisaema japonica?
questions.explanation: In Arisaema japonica, big roots that are rich in nutrients give female flowers.

questions.question: Favourable conditions produce which sex organs in Equisetum prothalli?
questions.explanation: Equisetum prothalli growing under favourable conditions produce female sex organs.

questions.question: The location of a gene on a sex chromosome is called which term?
questions.explanation: Sex linkage is the location of a gene on a sex chromosome.

questions.question: Genes found on the Y chromosome are referred to as which?
questions.explanation: Genes found on the Y chromosomes are referred to as Y-linked genes or holandric genes.

questions.question: Y-linked inheritance is transmitted from father to which offspring?
questions.explanation: Any Y-linked inheritance is transmitted from father to his sons.

questions.question: X-linked inheritance is transmitted by males to which offspring?
questions.explanation: Males transmit X-linked inheritance only to their daughters.

questions.question: Sons receive X-linked characters only from which parent?
questions.explanation: Sons receive X-linked characters only from their mothers.

questions.question: A lone X-linked gene in a male is referred to as which type?
questions.explanation: The lone X-linked gene in the male is referred to as a hemizygous gene.

questions.question: Why are males more likely to be affected by rare recessive disorders?
questions.explanation: Because males have a single copy of X-linked genes they are more likely to be affected by rare recessive disorders.

questions.question: In a cross between a normal female and a carrier male, which offspring are affected?
questions.explanation: When a normal female marries a carrier male for a disorder located on the X chromosome it is transmitted to all the male offspring.

questions.question: How many X-linked traits pass from a carrier male to daughters?
questions.explanation: In a situation where a carrier male mates with a normal female none of the X-linked traits are passed to the daughters.

questions.question: Hypertronic sweat is a symptom of which disease?
questions.explanation: Cystic Fibrosis is characterized by respiratory bronchiectasis, pancreatic insufficiency, and hypertronic sweat.

questions.question: De-pigmentation and pink eyes are symptoms of which disease?
questions.explanation: Albinism presents with de-pigmentation and pink eyes.

questions.question: Which condition presents with severe CNS defects and an odor of maple syrup?
questions.explanation: Maple Syrup Urine Disease presents with severe CNS defect, mental retardation, and the patient smells like maple syrup or burnt sugar.

questions.question: Sickle shaped red blood cells are a symptom of which disease?
questions.explanation: Sickle Cell Disease is characterized by sickle shaped red blood cells.

questions.question: Progressive dementia is a symptom of which disease?
questions.explanation: Huntington's Disease is an autosomal dominant disorder presenting with progressive dementia.

questions.question: Short-limbed dwarfism is a symptom of which disease?
questions.explanation: Achondroplasia presents with short-limbed dwarfism and an enlarged head.

questions.question: Which disorder presents with haemorrhage as a primary symptom?
questions.explanation: Von Willebrand Disease is an autosomal dominant disorder characterized by haemorrhage.

questions.question: A cat-like cry and microcephaly are symptoms of which syndrome?
questions.explanation: Cri du chat Syndrome presents with a cat-like cry, microcephaly, round-face, and wide-set eyes.
